architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Run at least 3 independent S1C41 preparations and calculate the mean 120-130 C level change relative to the matched unmodified reactive core. Accept exactly one registered hypothesis only if the mean change is within 3.40 percentage points of its prediction and the 95% uncertainty interval for the mean has a half-width no greater than 3.40 percentage points: H-LEVEL-DILUTE at -42.76%, H-LEVEL-ASSOC at 17.24%, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC at -72.76%.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary level observable is directly measured on the resin-modified S1C41 chemistry from 80 to 130 C and therefore does not depend on transfer of a rheological regularity from the unmodified chemistry family. The apparent E_eta descriptor is also measured from the candidate sweep, but remains a formulation-level regression descriptor. The binding audit marks M-SWEEP admissible; no unmodified shared-shape transfer is claimed.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the 95% uncertainty interval for the mean level change lies entirely outside [-46.16%, -39.36%]. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the interval lies entirely at or below 13.84%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if the interval lies entirely at or above -69.36%. If none of these conditions is met, no registered level hypothesis is falsified at the 3.40 percentage-point resolution because preparation-state uncertainty remains unresolved.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-REPEAT with at least 3 independently prepared samples and fully documented process history to quantify the realization-state spread, then repeat the direct S1C41::M-SWEEP if the state-control result shows that the level hypotheses can be resolved.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Mean directly measured viscosity level change relative to the matched unmodified reactive core at 120 C and 130 C, reported as percent, together with the directly measured 80-130 C viscosity curve.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41::M-SWEEP is the scientifically defensible experiment for the established failure mode because it directly measures the candidate processing-window viscosity rather than reconstructing it from an unvalidated shared shape. The binding audit excludes modified-chemistry M-ANCHOR cards, and I accept that restriction. The result can test the three registered formulation-level level predictions for the combined S1C41 formulation, but it cannot establish a molecular mechanism or isolate the individual modifier axes.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in retaining S1C41::M-SWEEP because it directly measures the decision quantity and is admissible under the binding chemistry audit. I followed the Skeptic in rejecting the original one-repeat interpretation of the 3.40% criterion: the execution is strengthened to at least 3 independent preparations with uncertainty-based adjudication. The deterministic tie was broken in favor of S1C41 because it is the lowest-acrylic-loading member of the tied, fully supported direct-sweep set while retaining the supported approximately 5% minor-resin level.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: S1C41 lies in the externally supported coarse region at 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor-tackifier-like modifier, but the exact AC1920/TK100 local response is unmeasured.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the primary observable because viscosity is measured directly over 80-130 C; high uncertainty remains only for any attempted transfer of the unmodified shared thermal-response shape or mechanistic interpretation.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The direct-sweep discrimination threshold is 3.40 percentage points, based on the catalogued direct-sweep residual; temperature-dependent instrument and fitting uncertainty affect the reported level and E_eta.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High and potentially dominant: the original matched-temperature preparations showed sample CV values of 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios up to 3.57 at 120 C. At least 3 independent candidate preparations are therefore required before applying the numerical hypothesis criteria.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original local PUR reactive-core formulation family represented by E1-E3, including the original modifier chemistry used in those measurements. The intended experiment should remain inside that chemistry family; any chemistry-changing modifier or reactive-core change must first pass the chemistry-domain applicability check, and one-point state calibration should not be used without that check.
planner.failure_mode: A modified reactive polyurethane hot-melt may miss the processing-viscosity window because its realized viscosity level is not known at the application temperatures.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E2 temperature sweep measured a viscosity decrease from a mean of 18530.7 at 80 C to 3322.0 at 130 C, while the three-run spread remained large (sample CV 0.46-0.58; max/min ratio 2.80-3.57). This establishes strong temperature dependence and substantial uncertainty in the realized level before any modifier effect is inferred.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local data measure temperature sweeps for original formulations E1-E3, but no modified candidate level is measured. The E2 level is also poorly resolved across preparations, with sample CV values of 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 over 80-130 C. The temperature response is sampled across six temperatures, whereas the candidate-specific level needed for the processing-window decision remains unknown.
measurement_requirements: Directly measure the candidate's viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared, fully documented sample rather than reconstructing the processing-window level from a single anchor.
Report the realized viscosity level at 120 and 130 C and the apparent temperature-response descriptor from ln(eta) versus 1/T.
Use sufficient independent repeats or state-control documentation to distinguish modifier-dependent level shifts from the observed local realization spread.

Compare the measured level against the frozen inert-dilution, acrylic-association, and plasticization predictions at matched temperature; the measurement must resolve differences below the catalogued 3.4% direct-sweep discrimination threshold where possible.
planner.scientific_question: At matched temperature and controlled process state, does the modified candidate's realized viscosity level follow inert dilution, rise above dilution because the acrylic-like modifier is associative, or fall below dilution because the modifiers form a plasticizing continuum?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The candidate chemistry is outside the measured unmodified chemistry family, so transfer of the local shared thermal-response shape is not assumed. The direct M-SWEEP remains admissible because it measures the candidate level and thermal response across 80-130 C rather than reconstructing the decision quantity from an anchor. The viscosity level is directly interpretable; the accompanying E_eta descriptor is obtained by regression and remains model-dependent.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If the measured 120-130 C level change falls within 3.40% of exactly one registered prediction—-42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC—that hypothesis is accepted for S1C41 and the measured processing-window level is reported with it.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured change is at or below the inert-dilution prediction of -42.76%; H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above -42.76%; and H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured change departs from -42.76% by more than 3.40%.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result not uniquely within 3.40% of one prediction does not support a registered level hypothesis at this resolution. It indicates overlap, unregistered modifier behavior, or unresolved process-state variation and requires cautious interpretation rather than forced assignment.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C, including the realized viscosity level at 120 and 130 C.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses a larger acrylic perturbation than necessary for the same direct three-hypothesis discrimination.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but its 20% acrylic loading is a larger intervention than the selected conservative lower-band candidate.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses a still larger acrylic loading and therefore a larger departure from the characterized reactive-core chemistry.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but combines the largest acrylic loading in the tied set with the same minor-tackifier loading, making it the least minimal tied intervention.

proposer.reasoning: The direct 80-130 C sweep addresses the least-resolved coordinate, the candidate processing-window viscosity level, and separates all three registered level hypotheses at the stated 3.40% resolution. It avoids the binding audit's inadmissible one-point anchor shortcut for modified chemistry. S1C41 is selected from the real VOI tie because it stays within the conservative externally supported intervention region while minimizing acrylic departure and retaining the supported 5% minor-tackifier level.
proposer.tie_break_justification: The deterministic VOI tool is indifferent among these five cards. S1C41 uses the lowest acrylic loading in the conservative externally supported 15-20% band while retaining the repeatedly supported approximately 5% minor-resin level. It therefore provides full three-hypothesis discrimination with the smallest justified intervention among the tied direct-sweep options.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: No change to the selected experiment. Retain the direct 80-130 C M-SWEEP for S1C41, but strengthen execution with at least three independent candidate preparations or repeated sweeps, documented process-state controls, and uncertainty-based reassessment of the 3.40% discrimination threshold.
residual_decision_risk: Preparation-state variation may remain large enough to prevent reliable separation of the registered level hypotheses.
The dual-axis S1C41 composition cannot isolate acrylic-like, minor-tackifier-like, or interaction effects from a single combined-formulation result.
The E_eta descriptor remains dependent on regression assumptions and may be affected by nonlinearity, drift, or unmeasured process-state displacement.

The modified resin chemistry is outside the measured unmodified shared-shape support; direct M-SWEEP is admissible and measures the primary level directly, but transfer of the prior shared thermal-response shape cannot be claimed without verification.
A stable transparent VOI ranking does not establish that S1C41 is scientifically correct or that its outcome will support a registered hypothesis.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is that the 3.40% acceptance or falsification threshold is not attainable with the specified minimum of one repeat, given the documented preparation spread of approximately 46-58% CV and a 3.57 max/min ratio at 120 C. This does not make M-SWEEP the wrong experiment: it still directly measures the candidate processing-window level and thermal response, unlike the inadmissible one-point anchor. It requires at least three independent preparations or equivalent repeated sweeps, documented process state, and recalculation of hypothesis resolution before assigning or falsifying a registered level hypothesis. The result should be interpreted as a combined-formulation level test, not as reliable isolation of individual modifier-axis effects or molecular mechanisms.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: S1C41::M-SWEEP is in the tied deterministic top set with S1C46::M-SWEEP, S1C51::M-SWEEP, S1C56::M-SWEEP, and S1C61::M-SWEEP. The top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, the base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower is 0.002292, and no recommendation_flip_boundary is reached for any weight term across the 0.5-1.5 sweep. Thus none of the evaluated defensible re-weightings changes the tied top set. The tie is scientifically resolved in favor of S1C41 because it uses the lowest acrylic loading in the supported 15-20% conservative band while retaining the repeatedly supported approximately 5% minor-resin loading.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary viscosity level observable stays inside direct measurement support because M-SWEEP measures the resin-modified S1C41 composition from 80-130 C and does not reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity from the unmodified shared shape. The proposal correctly marks shared_shape_use as verification_only. However, the prior shared thermal-response shape was measured only in unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry and cannot support transfer claims for S1C41 until the direct sweep, preferably with independent repeats and documented process state, demonstrates the candidate response.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol cannot reliably meet the 3.40% criterion as specified. M-SWEEP requires only one repeat, while the original matched-temperature preparation spread is approximately 46-58% CV and reaches a 3.57 max/min ratio at 120 C. The prior 3.4% multiplicative RMSE describes a fitted direct-sweep geometry and is not a demonstrated candidate-level repeatability limit. Multiple independent preparations and repeated candidate sweeps are required before a 3.40% departure can be treated as falsification.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may label H-LEVEL-DILUTE falsified, or accept one of the alternative hypotheses, when the observed difference is actually caused by preparation-state variation.
objections.objection: The stated 3.40% falsification/acceptance resolution for M-SWEEP is not attainable with the specified minimum of one repeat. The original E2 repeatability data show sample CV values of 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 over 80-130 C, including a 3.57 ratio at 120 C. The 3.40% threshold is based on a prior shared-shape fit residual, not on the candidate's preparation and measurement uncertainty. A single freshly prepared candidate sweep therefore cannot establish that a departure from the -42.76% inert-dilution prediction is greater than 3.40%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The claim that S1C41 can distinguish all three level hypotheses at the registered resolution remains unsupported even though their idealized prediction intervals do not overlap.
objections.objection: The numerical predictions for S1C41 are separated by more than 3.40% (-72.76%, -42.76% and 17.24%), so the direct observable nominally covers the three registered level hypotheses. However, the experiment does not separate those predictions from the documented realization spread: the protocol has min_repeats 1, process_state_risk_score 0.75, and six missing process fields. Thus the claimed full discrimination score of 1.0 in hypothesis_discrimination_detail is a resolution calculation, not evidence that the protocol can resolve the hypotheses in practice.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any conclusion about which modifier axis or mechanism caused the observed level shift would be unsupported; only a phenomenological result for the combined S1C41 formulation could be claimed.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15.0% and TK100 is 5.0%, with reactive_mass_fraction 0.8. A single level result cannot attribute any departure from dilution to the acrylic-like axis, the minor-tackifier-like axis, or their interaction. In particular, H-LEVEL-ASSOC depends on acrylic_like while H-LEVEL-PLASTIC depends on the total of both axes; the dual-axis composition can test whole-formulation level predictions, but it cannot isolate acrylic association from tackifier plasticization.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct level result may remain usable, but any claim that the sweep establishes a transferable or mechanistically meaningful thermal-response descriptor would be weaker than stated.
objections.objection: The viscosity level at 120 and 130 C is directly measured by M-SWEEP, so the primary level observable is stronger than M-ANCHOR. However, the primary observable is paired with E_eta obtained by regressing ln(eta) against 1/T, and the catalog explicitly gives the sweep interpretability as 0.7 because the response descriptor inherits regression assumptions. The protocol does not specify how nonlinearity, drift during the sweep, or preparation-state displacement will be separated from a temperature-response effect.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Acceptance of H-LEVEL-ASSOC or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC could be overinterpreted as proof of a molecular mechanism that the planned rheology does not measure.
objections.objection: The registry correctly limits the hypotheses to formulation-level viscosity statements, but the names and interpretation of H-LEVEL-ASSOC and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC can be read as molecular mechanism claims. A viscosity sweep alone cannot establish association, a plasticizing continuum, or any molecular interaction; it only tests whether the measured level lies above or below the registered phenomenological prediction.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain the direct M-SWEEP but require at least three independent candidate preparations and report the between-preparation spread at 120 and 130 C; add the admissible M-REPEAT state-control measurement or an equivalent repeated-sweep protocol. Recalculate the hypothesis resolution from the combined candidate and reference uncertainty before applying the 3.40% acceptance or falsification threshold. Interpret the result as a combined-formulation level test, not as isolation of the AC1920 or TK100 mechanism.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The stated 3.40% falsification/acceptance resolution for M-SWEEP is not attainable with the specified minimum of one repeat. The original E2 repeatability data show sample CV values of 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 over 80-130 C, including a 3.57 ratio at 120 C. The 3.40% threshold is based on a prior shared-shape fit residual, not on the candidate's preparation and measurement uncertainty. A single freshly prepared candidate sweep therefore cannot establish that a departure from the -42.76% inert-dilution prediction is greater than 3.40%.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: The audited upstream material structure and chemistry support boundary are required before candidate or experiment ranking and before using any local rheological regularity.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: Return the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis and registered formulation axes needed to frame the direct level-discrimination experiment without using post-result information.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

measurement_plan.name: 80-130 C temperature sweep
measurement_plan.primary_observable: directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T
measurement_plan.protocol: Measure viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample and regress ln(eta) against 1/T.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: The measured 120-130 C level change against the unmodified reactive core falls within 3.40% of exactly one registered prediction: -38.18% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 21.82% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC or -64.43% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. That hypothesis is accepted for this composition and the processing-window level is reported with it.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The 80-130 C sweep is the direct verification measurement that establishes the thermal-response shape for a chemistry-shifted candidate.
